goal: Let node operators and researchers see how much CPU each peer's message processing consumes
Lays groundwork for possible future CPU-aware peer prioritization or DoS defenses
reviewability: Paused: sipa and ajtowns raised unresolved design objections since author's last reply in April 2026
Their concerns could change the PR's shape entirely, so waiting on author before further review pays off
agreement: Disputed: early concept and tested ACKs exist but later design objections remain unanswered
Strong support because it surfaces useful per-peer CPU disparities (jonatack, yuvicc)
Verified by testing the metric behaves sensibly in practice (0xB10C, BrandonOdiwuor)
Unaddressed objection: doubts the field belongs in production getpeerinfo, suggests experimental RPC instead (sipa)
Unaddressed objection: metric isn't actionable or comparable across peers (ajtowns)

categories.name: rpc
why: P3 because it's a new optional backwards-compatible field with contested but real value
Some reviewers found it useful for spotting expensive peers, others doubt its actionability or fit in a stable RPC
Demand is mostly internal and exploratory rather than from external API consumers

categories.name: p2p
why: P3 because it only adds visibility into per-peer CPU cost, not an actual defense mechanism
Framed by a reviewer as a useful first step toward anti-DoS measures, but the future payoff is uncertain
Other reviewers doubt this exact metric will end up being the one used for that eventual purpose

categories.name: utils
why: P4 because the new CPU-timer utility has only one consumer, the feature added in this same PR
Not a broadly reused pattern, so its leverage beyond this PR is limited
